report.tagline: A UK buy now, pay later card and app that works almost anywhere Mastercard is accepted, kept cheap for shoppers by brand deals and advertising.
report.simpleSummary: Zilch is a card and app that lets you split a purchase into smaller payments. Most buy now, pay later services only work at certain shops, but the Zilch card works almost anywhere that takes Mastercard, online or in store. You can pay in full and get cashback, or split into four payments over six weeks with no interest. Zilch keeps costs low for shoppers by earning money from brands that pay to reach its users, a bit like how Google is free because advertisers pay.

keyNumbers.note: Tech.eu gives £35.8 to £35.9 million, up from £12.5 million, due to marketing and higher credit loss provisions on longer loans. Zilch reports two quarters in a row of adjusted profit before tax.

overview.whatItDoes: Zilch gives shoppers a card and app to pay in full with cashback or split payments, plus longer loans for bigger buys. It is authorised by the FCA as a consumer credit firm. It earns from brand commissions and ads, card fees, small fees on some splits and interest on longer loans. In January 2026 it agreed to buy Fjord Bank in Poland to expand into Europe.
howItWorks: You download the app, pass identity and credit checks and get a spending limit.
You add the Zilch card to Apple Pay or Google Pay, or get a physical card.
At checkout, you choose to pay in full with cashback, or split into four payments: 25% today and the rest over six weeks.
At partner brands, Zilch earns a commission from the brand and passes some back to you as extra rewards.
Brands pay to show deals in the app, reaching shoppers at the moment they are ready to buy.
Longer loans let you spread bigger buys over months, with interest.
overview.valueProposition: Flexible payments and cashback almost anywhere, with no interest on pay in 4, paid for mainly by brands rather than shoppers.

steps.detail: Watches a TikTok about paying in 4 anywhere and installs Zilch.
Passes identity and credit checks in minutes.

Splits an £80 jacket into four £20 payments, paying £20 today.
Pays the other £60 over six weeks by automatic card payments.
Gets a higher limit after repaying on time.

Cashback appears in the app as rewards.
Uses the rewards on the next purchase.

businessModel.summary: Zilch makes money from brands (commissions and ads), interchange on card spending, small fees on some split payments, and interest on longer loans. The idea is that brands pay so shoppers do not have to.

revenueStreams.detail: Brands pay Zilch for sales it sends them and for showing offers in the app.
A small fee the shop's bank pays each time the Zilch card is used.
A small fee on some split payments at non-partner shops.
Interest on longer loans for bigger purchases.

businessModel.pricing: Free to download and use. Pay in 4 is interest-free. A small fee may apply when splitting at non-partner shops. Longer loans charge interest. Fees change, so check the app for current terms.
costDrivers: Credit losses on unpaid splits and loans, which rose with longer loans in FY26
Marketing and brand building to win users
Funding costs for the money it lends
businessModel.unitEconomics: An active user spends about £2,500 a year with Zilch. Revenue of £147.5 million on £2.4 billion of spending is about 6%, so roughly £150 a year per active user. Credit losses, funding and card costs take a large part of that. The FY26 loss of about £36 million spread across 970,000 active users means Zilch lost about £37 per active user in the year after marketing. Growing brand revenue per user, which costs almost nothing to serve, is how Zilch plans to make a profit.

growth.moat: Weak to moderate. The ad-subsidised model and the 'use anywhere' card are different, but bigger players like Klarna have copied a card product. Zilch's main assets are its spending data on young UK shoppers, which brands pay to reach, and its brand relationships.

pmLessons: Who pays matters. Zilch tries to make brands pay so shoppers do not have to.
Registered users are not active users; build metrics around activity.
Longer loans grow revenue but raise risk; always pair growth metrics with loss metrics.
Being different from the leader, here with a 'use anywhere' card, can win a niche.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Zilch's ad revenue without annoying users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find what brands want (reach, proven sales) and what users want (useful deals). Build relevant offers. Measure revenue per user and app satisfaction.

interviewQuestions.question: How do you turn registered users into active ones?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find where users drop off: limit too low, no card in wallet, forgot. Use offers and onboarding fixes. Track activation rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Zilch vs Klarna: how should Zilch compete?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a niche: use anywhere, cashback, UK young shoppers. Avoid matching Klarna's merchant network head-on.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you manage credit risk on longer loans?
interviewQuestions.hint: Better checks, lower starting limits, early warnings, help for users who miss payments. Guardrail: default rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star metric would you pick for Zilch?
interviewQuestions.hint: Active users who repay on time. Explain why sign-ups or GMV alone mislead.
